meta.title: Getting a therapeutic into the living human brain
meta.question: For each route past the blood-brain barrier: how far has it actually been shown to work, and in whom?
meta.verification: Every record was sourced by web-search agents against primary sources and has NOT yet been hand-checked by a human. Treat as a well-sourced draft, not a finished record.
meta.engine: claim-evidence-grading v0 (shared with ssmt, gomin) — a claim graded on an evidence ladder + what was measured + independent replication + drift

ladder.label: proposed
ladder.blurb: an idea or mechanism on paper; nothing built

ladder.label: in a dish
ladder.blurb: works in cultured cells or an organoid

ladder.label: in a rodent
ladder.blurb: works in a living mouse or rat

ladder.label: in a large animal
ladder.blurb: works in a non-human primate or comparable model

ladder.label: in humans, once
ladder.blurb: shown in people by a single group, usually the originator

ladder.label: in humans, independently
ladder.blurb: reproduced in people by a group with no stake in the claim

measuredLegend.function: changed a person's life (motor milestones, survival, tumour response)
measuredLegend.biomarker: moved a surrogate number (CSF sugar, plaque, nerve protein) without proven clinical benefit
measuredLegend.opening: demonstrated the barrier opens, not that a delivered drug helped
measuredLegend.access: showed the agent reaches CSF/tissue, not a clinical outcome
measuredLegend.transduction: showed cells were reached/expressed, not a clinical outcome
measuredLegend.none: no clinical or surrogate benefit demonstrated

families.through: Through the barrier — reach brain cells from the bloodstream (the dream)
families.around: Around the barrier — bypass it with a needle or physical opening (where the results are)

records.subject: Engineered AAV capsid, IV (PHP.B family)
records.claim: an engineered virus injected into a vein crosses the blood-brain barrier and broadly transduces the brain
records.rungCeilingNote: L2 for the capability everyone cites (mouse); an L3 record of FAILURE sits above it (primate IV)
records.replicationNote: mouse effect reproduced by Hordeaux (UPenn) and Batista (UMass); primate IV failure reproduced by three unaffiliated groups
records.keyEvidence: ~10,000x better mouse-brain delivery than AAV9; mechanism runs through the LY6A receptor, which humans do not have; failed primate IV transduction in 3 independent NHP studies; next-gen CAP-B10/B22 failed an independent 2025 marmoset re-test. Exactly one human ever IV-dosed an engineered BBB capsid (Capsida CAP-002); that child died, trial terminated, sister program withdrawn.
records.drift: 'a virus that crosses the blood-brain barrier' — via a receptor humans lack, failed in every independent primate test, with one human exposure that ended in death

citations.ref: Liguore et al. (macaque IT vs IV)

records.precision: The Capsida trial pause was the company's own; no public document establishes the later regulatory hold as FDA-imposed — do not claim it was.

records.subject: Human-TfR-targeted AAV capsid (BI-hTFR1)
records.claim: a capsid aimed at a receptor humans DO have crosses the human BBB
records.keyEvidence: works in humanized-TfR knock-in mice (L2) and human brain endothelial cells (L1); cannot be tested in wild-type NHP; no independent replication located.
records.drift: promising engineering answer to the LY6A problem, with zero human data

records.subject: Systemic AAV9, IV (onasemnogene abeparvovec / Zolgensma)
records.claim: IV AAV9 transduces human CNS neurons
records.replicationNote: human CNS transduction shown in a single sponsor-affiliated n=2 autopsy study
records.keyEvidence: clinical benefit in SMA is real and replicated; but direct human CNS transduction rests on 2 deceased infants, with liver vector 300-1000x higher than CNS.
records.drift: 'proves IV AAV9 transduces human CNS' rests on two autopsies; clinical benefit is offered as transduction evidence but is not

records.subject: TfR receptor-mediated transcytosis (tividenofusp / Denali)
records.claim: an enzyme ferried across the BBB on the transferrin receptor treats neurologic Hunter syndrome
records.replicationNote: concept cross-confirmed by JCR's independent TfR construct
records.keyEvidence: approval rests on a 91% drop in CSF heparan sulfate (a surrogate); the confirmatory trial for cognitive benefit (COMPASS) is still running; no human measurement of enzyme in brain parenchyma.
records.drift: 'a drug that crosses the BBB and treats neurologic Hunter' — what was shown is a CSF sugar falling, with no proven cognitive benefit

records.subject: TfR fusion (pabinafusp / JCR)
records.claim: an anti-TfR antibody-enzyme fusion crosses the BBB for MPS II
records.keyEvidence: n=28, CSF heparan sulfate reduction; cognitive improvement claimed only in a post-hoc, open-label subgroup treated before significant neuronopathy.
records.drift: an approval on a Japanese priority pathway with n=28 and a biomarker co-primary, read as proof RMT delivers to human brain

records.subject: Brainshuttle antibody (trontinemab / Roche)
records.claim: a shuttle antibody delivers 10-50x more antibody into the human brain
records.keyEvidence: Phase 3, not approved; clears amyloid plaque on PET (-107 centiloids at wk 28) at low ARIA; only direct human exposure number is CSF:plasma 0.8%; no evidence yet it slows cognitive decline.
records.drift: 'Brainshuttle validated' — the 10-50x brain-uptake figure is a mouse/NHP number; the human data are one CSF ratio and a plaque-clearance PD response

records.subject: Lipid nanoparticles to the brain, systemic
records.claim: LNPs injected into the bloodstream deliver to the brain
records.replicationNote: rodent brain delivery reported by several unaffiliated labs; no human data
records.keyEvidence: rodent only; no human data and no registered human trial for brain delivery; the one human GBM LNP trial (n=3) works via peripheral immune signalling, not BBB crossing.
records.drift: 'LNPs can now cross the BBB' describes reporter mRNA in mouse brain

records.subject: Intranasal / nose-to-brain
records.claim: a drug sniffed in travels up the olfactory nerves straight to the brain
records.rungCeilingNote: L4 for trace, variable CSF access; no functional benefit
records.replicationNote: the strongest recent independent human quantitative attempt was negative
records.keyEvidence: theory is mostly rodent-inferred; the large human functional test (intranasal insulin for Alzheimer's, SNIFF, n=289) was null (P=.98); esketamine works by ordinary systemic absorption and is not nose-to-brain evidence.
records.drift: 'bypasses the BBB via olfactory pathways' — human data support only trace, highly variable CSF appearance, not meaningful parenchymal concentration

records.subject: Engineered exosomes / extracellular vesicles
records.claim: exosomes are a natural vehicle that carries cargo into the brain
records.replicationNote: Primate study found EVs in CSF at 30-60 min post-IV but minimal brain parenchymal accumulation.
records.keyEvidence: rodent evidence; negative primate result; no approvals; registry-only clinical footprint; FDA safety notice on unapproved exosome products.
records.drift: a preclinical platform presented as clinical-stage

records.subject: Intrathecal ASO (nusinersen / Spinraza)
records.claim: an antisense oligonucleotide in the spinal fluid treats a CNS disease
records.rungCeilingNote: L5 for real function — but the disease sits in the spinal cord, not the brain
records.keyEvidence: real, independently replicated improvement in children's motor milestones; but human autopsy shows a steep caudo-rostral gradient — plenty in the lumbar spine, little by the cortex.
records.drift: cited as proof of 'CNS-wide ASO delivery'; human tissue shows a spinal-cord-weighted gradient

records.subject: Intrathecal ASO (tofersen / Qalsody)
records.claim: an intrathecal ASO treats genetic ALS
records.keyEvidence: approved on a nerve-damage biomarker; the Phase 3 VALOR trial missed its clinical endpoint.
records.drift: 'ASOs work in ALS' — what was shown is biomarker engagement without a met clinical endpoint

records.subject: ICV enzyme replacement (cerliponase alfa / Brineura)
records.claim: enzyme delivered into the brain's ventricles distributes through the brain
records.keyEvidence: independently shown to slow the brain disease; but the children's retinas degenerate on schedule, untouched — the enzyme poured into the centre of the brain never reaches them.
records.drift: 'ICV distributes enzyme through the brain' — the retinal finding is the cleanest human proof of incomplete reach
records.replicationNote: Both supporting studies share a senior author and group (Schulz, Hamburg) — not an independent replication. Rung lowered 2026-07-27.

records.subject: Direct intraparenchymal gene therapy (eladocagene / Kebilidi / Upstaza)
records.claim: a gene therapy injected straight into brain tissue works
records.replicationNote: the ROUTE is independently supported (Bankiewicz n=7, different product); the product is not replicated

approvals.note: first gene therapy administered directly to the brain in the US

records.keyEvidence: a virus infused into one deep structure (the putamen); precise, single-shot, never repeated; covers one nucleus plus projections, essentially zero distal distribution.
records.drift: usable only for the rare diseases whose whole problem sits in one anatomically defined place

records.subject: Focused ultrasound + microbubbles (BBB opening)
records.claim: focused ultrasound gets drugs into the brain and extends survival
records.rungCeilingNote: L5 for OPENING the barrier — not for any delivery outcome
records.replicationNote: opening confirmed in humans by at least six unaffiliated groups
records.keyEvidence: reversible, repeatable, safe BBB opening is proven in humans; whether a drug pushed through the opening improves an outcome has NOT been shown in a randomized trial (SONOBIRD, n=560, reports ~end-2026).
records.drift: 'FUS delivers drugs and extends survival' — the opening is proven; the outcome RCT does not yet exist

records.subject: Convection-enhanced delivery (catheter under pressure)
records.claim: a pressurized catheter delivers drug through the tissue to the target
records.rungCeilingNote: L4/L5 with NEGATIVE outcome — both adequately powered trials failed
records.replicationNote: no independently replicated positive outcome; the powered trials were negative
records.keyEvidence: decades of human use; the powered brain-cancer trial (PRECISE) and the powered Parkinson's GDNF trial both missed their endpoints; a blinded audit found ~half the PRECISE catheters misplaced — the study may have tested a drug it never delivered.
records.drift: 'CED bypasses the BBB and delivers to the target' — bypass is real; verified coverage is the unsolved problem

records.subject: Locoregional CAR-T (into the ventricle / tumour cavity)
records.claim: engineered immune cells reach and treat brain tumours
records.rungCeilingNote: L5 for the ROUTE (ICV/intracavitary); efficacy per target not independently replicated
records.replicationNote: the locoregional route is replicated across four unaffiliated centres; target-specific efficacy is not
records.keyEvidence: the strongest functional responses on the map — tumour shrinkage and neurological improvement — for childhood brainstem tumours and glioblastoma, delivered directly into the ventricles or cavity; the one IV trial with tissue data showed cells trafficked into the brain but produced no responses and the worst toxicity.
records.drift: 'CAR-T reaches brain tumours' omits that every responding programme injects into the ventricle/cavity; IV dosing caused the DLTs, not the responses
